name: monarchTextStyle(_:)
title: Heading
summary: A heading is a Text with one of the heading roles of monarchTextStyle(_:) and the header trait. Monarch ships no separate heading type.
whenToUse: For the title of a screen, a section or a card. Choose the role by how large the heading should look: display, title, heading, subheading, bodyStrong or label.
whenNotToUse: Not for the title in a navigation bar; set navigationTitle and leave it to the system. Not for emphasis inside running text; use bodyStrong without the header trait.
api: func monarchTextStyle(_ style: MonarchTextStyle) -> some View

options.name: style
options.description: The look. display is the web size 4xl, title 2xl, heading xl, subheading lg, bodyStrong base and label sm.

states.name: one line
states.description: lineLimit(1) keeps the heading to one line and ends it with an ellipsis.

appearance: The role sets size, weight, tracking and line spacing; display and title are set tight. The modifier sets no colour: a heading takes the default text colour of the theme, or the muted text colour for a secondary heading.
platformNotes: The web Heading sets the outline level (h1 to h6) and the visual size separately. iOS has no document outline: the header trait makes a text a heading for VoiceOver, and accessibilityHeading(_:) adds a level (h1 to h6) for the rotor when a screen has nested sections. The web sizes 3xl and 5xl have no role; display (4xl) is the nearest. The web weight option is not offered: the role decides the weight. Tone and truncation are the standard foregroundStyle and lineLimit. Android covers this with MonarchText.
accessibility: accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) lets VoiceOver users move between headings with the rotor.
accessibilityHeading(_:) gives the heading a level from h1 to h6; without it the level is unspecified.
Every role scales with Dynamic Type, including the accessibility sizes.
A heading wraps by default, so no text is lost at large sizes.
edgeCases: The role does not make a text a heading for VoiceOver; the trait must be added.
With lineLimit(1) the cut-off part is still read by VoiceOver, because the label is the whole text.
Text balancing (the web text-wrap: balance) is not available in SwiftUI.

examples.title: Levels and their default sizes
examples.code:
VStack(alignment: .leading) {
    Text("Workspace overview")
        .monarchTextStyle(.title)
        .accessibilityHeading(.h1)
    Text("Recent activity")
        .monarchTextStyle(.heading)
        .accessibilityHeading(.h2)
    Text("This week")
        .monarchTextStyle(.subheading)
        .accessibilityHeading(.h3)
    Text("Pinned items")
        .monarchTextStyle(.bodyStrong)
        .accessibilityHeading(.h4)
}
